# Executive decision presentation scenario

Use this scenario when executives or accountable sponsors must approve an
investment, architecture, roadmap, policy, or delivery decision.

- Working title: <presentation title>
- Audience: <decision-makers and prior knowledge>
- Decision required: <one explicit approval or choice>
- Decision deadline: <date or meeting>
- Current audience position: <what they believe or question now>
- Intended final position: <what they should believe and do>
- Target slide count: <count or range>

## Scenario arc

| Stage | Audience question | Assertion to establish | Required evidence | Transition to next stage | Suggested slides |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Context | Why does this require attention now? | <change, deadline, or opportunity makes action timely> | <external change, KPI, commitment> | If action is timely, show the consequence of inaction | 1–2 |
| Tension | What happens if we continue as-is? | <current state creates measurable cost, risk, or delay> | <baseline, incident, trend, user impact> | Once the gap is credible, define the decision criteria | 1–2 |
| Criteria | How should the options be judged? | <shared cost, value, risk, and feasibility criteria> | <constraints, targets, policy> | Compare options using the agreed criteria | 1 |
| Options | What choices are realistically available? | <credible alternatives include the status quo> | <comparable analysis> | Identify the option that best satisfies the criteria | 1–2 |
| Recommendation | What should we choose and why? | <recommended option delivers the best justified outcome> | <benefits, trade-offs, TCO, evidence> | Show that execution risk is controlled | 1–2 |
| Plan | Can this be delivered safely? | <owners, milestones, controls, and rollback make delivery feasible> | <roadmap, staffing, risk controls> | Convert confidence into a precise decision | 1–2 |
| Decision | What exactly must be approved today? | <specific approval, funding, owner, and next checkpoint> | <decision wording and consequences> | End with the requested action | 1 |

## Scenario acceptance checks

- Reading only the assertions forms a complete decision argument.
- The status quo and at least one alternative use the same evaluation axes.
- Benefits, cost, risks, and delivery controls are evidence-based.
- The final stage asks for one explicit decision with an owner and deadline.
